question.leadin: Answer the following about emperors of Japan.
question.text: This man has the distinction of maintaining the longest reign of any Japanese emperor. He is more famously known for overseeing the Japanese surrender during World War II.
question.clue: This ruler, who delivered the Jewel Voice Broadcast, later renounced his divinity in the Humanity Declaration.

swap.leadin: The final holder of this title was Tokugawa Yoshinobu.
swap.text: Prior to an 1868 restoration of imperial rule, what title was held by military rulers of Japan?
swap.clue: Two successive dynasties in this position supported the illegitimate Northern Court.

question.leadin: Give the following about surprise attacks in Japanese history.
question.text: In the 1560 Battle of Okehazama, this daimyo's forces sneaked to the rear of the opposing army, killing the opposing leader at his tent. This unifier of Japan was succeeded by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu.
question.clue: This huge fan of the Tanegashima rifle once won a battle by arranging his arquebusiers into three rows.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Japanese history.
swap.text: This victor of Sekigahara created that new shogunate and moved the capital from Kyoto to Edo, soon renamed Tokyo. His line would rule as shogun until the Meiji Restoration
swap.clue: After being designated Hideyori's regent, he defeated Ishida Mitsunari's Eastern Army at Sekigahara.

question.leadin: To fill the power void left by the fall of the Tokugawa bakufu, this ruler promulgated the Charter Oath and established a strong central government.
question.text: Name this man, who oversaw Japan's modernization efforts from 1868 to 1912 as emperor.
question.answerHtml: Emperor Meiji [or Meiji-tennō; accept Mutsuhito; accept Meiji the Great; or Meiji-taitei]
question.clue: He received support from the daimyos of Choshu and Satsuma in taking power.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about sarin attacks.
swap.text: This religious cult launched a sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway in 1995, killing 13 passengers. After the arrest of its leader Shoko Asahara, this group has rebranded itself as Aleph.
swap.clue: They believe that America is the Beast of revelation mentioned in the Bible, and that a war between the US and this religion's native country will lead to Armageddon.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the history of Christianity in Asia.
question.text: This Japanese shogunate, named after the victor at the Battle of Sekigahara, crushed the Shimabara Rebellion which was led by peasant Catholics. It also forced suspected kirishitan to step on fumi-e, or images of Jesus or Mary.
question.clue: This clan adopted sakoku until the arrival of the "black ships" of Matthew Perry.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese history prior to the Meiji Restoration.
swap.text: This city was the capital of Japan until Emperor Meiji made Tokyo the capital in 1868.
swap.clue: The historic shrines and religious landmarks of this city survive today because Henry Stimson prevented it from being targeted with the atomic bomb.

question.text: This first Shogunate began after Minamoto Yoritomo defeated the Tairas at the Battle of Dannoura in 1185. It was late dominated by the Hojo family.
question.clue: Before a major battle one leader of this polity meditated to find the source of cowardice in himself, and one conflict during it occurred when the cloistered emperor Go-Toba attempted to take the throne.

swap.leadin: Its seven virtues included courage, honor and respect.
swap.text: Identify this honor code followed by the forty-seven ronin when they avenged the death of Asano Naganori.
swap.clue: After the Tokugawa unification, literature on this subject shifted away from swordsmanship to more general philosophical principles. This Japanese word refers to the moral code and practices of samurai.

question.leadin: During this period, emperors who retired to monasteries retained power in the system of cloistered rule.
question.text: Name this period that succeeded the Nara Period. This period came to an end with the Genpei War.
question.clue: Go-Sanjo and Shirawaka established the "cloistered emperor" or "insei" system during this period, which was dominated by the Fujiwara clan.

swap.text: After the Genpei War, Minamoto Yoritomo founded the first instance of this form of Japanese dictatorship, named for its capital at Kamakura. Later instances of this form of government were named for Ashikaga and Tokugawa.
swap.clue: One dynasty of this rank was founded after the Battle of Sekigahara and ordered subordinates to leave their families in Edo as hostages.

question.leadin: The "affliction of abiding in ignorance," meaning the absence of enlightenment, is compared to the act of "stopping" in this practice in the first section of the manual The Unfettered Mind.
question.text: Name this activity, whose central object is referred to as "life-giving" in a treatise on it translated by William Scott Wilson. This activity is the primary subject of Miyamoto Musashi's The Book of Five Rings.
question.answerHtml: swordfighting [or swordsmanship; or kenjutsu; prompt on martial arts; prompt on dueling]

swap.leadin: It featured the Kitayama and the Higashiyama cultures and was founded by Takauji.
swap.text: Name this period of Japanese history that began with the Northern and Southern Courts period and which followed the Kamakura as the second shogunate.
swap.clue: This period saw a conflict between Yamana Sozen and Hosokawa Katsumoto, and was preceded by a three year period where Emperor Go-Daigo attempted to restore imperial power called the Kemmu restoration.

question.leadin: These laws brought about the development of estates called shoen.
question.text: Name this set of laws promulgated during the Asuka period, which curtailed the power of regional governors and imported traditions like the equal field system from China.
question.clue: The Asuka period ended with this set of reforms promulgated by the Kotoku Emperor which centralized power and introduced reorganization based on Tang Chinese lines.

swap.leadin: The massive temple complex of Todai-ji was constructed during this period as the center of a system of provincial temples known as kokubun-ji.
swap.text: Name this period of Japanese history in the 8th century that began with the establishment of Heijo-kyo as the capital. This period was followed by the Heian ("HAY-on") period.
swap.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

question.leadin: Unlike the Gishi Wajinden, this chronicle makes little mention of Empress Himiko, a semi-mythical shaman queen who established relations with Cao Wei ("tsao way").
question.text: Name this work, which was completed eight years after the Kojiki and chronicles national myths and history up to the 8th century.
question.clue: This set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.

swap.text: With the Asuka Period, the Kofun Period forms part of this period of Japanese history when the imperial capital was at Nara. This period shares its name with Japan's primary ethnic group and with the Japanese battleship that was the country's flagship for most of World War Two.

question.text: The foremost predecessor of the LDP was the Liberal Party, which was led by this towering figure of post-WWII Japanese politics. He served as Prime Minister five times between 1946 and 1954, and formulated a namesake Doctrine for Japan's postwar recovery.

swap.text: Although it is an independent corporation, Sony is associated with Sumitomo Mitsui, one of these horizontally integrated conglomerates. These conglomerates took a leading role in the Japanese economy after the postwar dissolution of the zaibatsu.
